name: Downtify
description: Downtify is a self-hosted music downloader with a web interface. Paste a Spotify, YouTube Music or Deezer link, or search by name, and it reads the metadata without a Spotify account or API key, downloads the matching audio from YouTube Music with yt-dlp and tags it with cover art and lyrics. It also has a library with a built-in player, a Playlist Monitor that downloads new tracks from watched playlists and artists, podcasts, M3U export for Jellyfin, Navidrome and Plex, and accounts for several users.

notes.text: Every Downtify server starts with the same login, admin / downtify. Change the password right after the first sign-in in Settings > General > Account. If you forget it, reset it to the default with: cd /opt/downtify && set -a && . /opt/downtify_data/.env && set +a && .venv/bin/python main.py auth-reset

Downtify serves plain HTTP on port 8000. Do not expose it to the internet directly; put it behind a reverse proxy with HTTPS. Add the proxy's address as DOWNTIFY_TRUSTED_PROXIES=<ip> to /opt/downtify_data/.env and have the proxy send X-Forwarded-Host/-Proto/-For, otherwise Downtify answers "Cross-site request refused" when the proxy rewrites the Host header, and rate-limits sign-ins by the proxy's address.

Music is saved to /opt/downtify_data/downloads. To keep it on a NAS or share it with a media server, bind-mount that folder from the host, e.g. pct set <CTID> -mp0 /mnt/media/music,mp=/opt/downtify_data/downloads. In an unprivileged container the host folder must be writable by UID 100000.

Settings, accounts, the Playlist Monitor database and an uploaded cookies.txt live in /opt/downtify_data/data, outside the app directory, so updates keep them. Optional variables from the documentation (TZ, DOWNTIFY_MONITOR_SYNC_TIME, DOWNTIFY_FORCE_IPV4, ...) go in /opt/downtify_data/.env, followed by systemctl restart downtify.
If YouTube starts refusing downloads ("Sign in to confirm you're not a bot", age-restricted tracks), upload a cookies.txt from a logged-in browser in Settings > YouTube cookies.
Downtify downloads the audio from YouTube. Whether that is allowed depends on YouTube's terms of service and the law where you live.
